note: agent-decomposed 2026-09-22 (stasis round 3) from §6 sequencing (1-5) + §3a-§3e decisions + §5 boundaries. The verdict (SSR aligned; the gap is the developer-half delivery contract) is settled. Step 1 (URLSearchParams shim conformance) is evidenced in elohim-render/src/shim/url.js; no manifest 'delivery' schema fields yet; render-path logic (trust-scoped cache, gating) still lives doorway-side (doorway ssr.rs, cache/store.rs), so the zero-doorway mesh test does not hold yet.

items.text: Step 1a: SSR-stall fix — URLSearchParams.sort() shim conformance in elohim-render (first instance of the env contract)
items.note: elohim-render/src/shim/url.js carries the URLSearchParams shim; verify sort() coverage by test.

items.text: Step 1b: isolate-reuse trust-boundary settlement (realm-per-render or equivalent) before any per-user credentialed SSR

Step 2 / §3e: move render serving logic (trust-scoped cache, capability derivation, auth-mode gating, shed taxonomy) out of doorway into the shared engine/render-host layer; doorway and storage-ssr become symmetric thin hosts
Acceptance for step 2: a mesh with zero doorways has full SSR delivery among render-capable peers (a2o)
Step 3 / §3a: app-manifest delivery section — browser bundle CID, optional server bundle CID (= SSR-capable marker), render spec as a matching key; schema -> contract test -> TS codegen
Step 4 / §3b: versioned render-host environment contract (shim surface, fetch routing rule, stability semantics) stamped beside RenderSpec; a2o compose/capability features assert it
§3d framework pluggability: native-Rust content body renderer registered as another renderer id against the same manifest declaration
Step 5: cross-peer render delegation on delegates-compute, only when a real second-peer use case exists
